title: Choose CoffeeWorks' visual world
question: Each card shows the Live Brew Station on an iPad mid-pour. Keep the roll, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Roaster's Label
options.lineage: Specialty roaster bag labels and roast cards
options.thesis: Every recipe is printed like the bag it came from: a flat colour slab, a lot number, a spec block.
options.viewport: Left rail of disciplines; the active recipe fills the header as its label colour with lot no. CW-014; timer and scale read huge beside a pour schedule drawn to time scale.
options.risk: Six discipline colours can turn into a toy box if more than one fills a screen at once.

raised.raise: One grotesk carries everything from the 120px timer to 11px spec labels, on a 1px hairline grid.
Pour schedules are drawn to time scale: a stage's width is its exact duration.
Done steps are struck through like printed marks, never faded.
Beans form a finite roster ranked by rest window, each with its roast 'birthday' and one-line note.
Every recipe, bean and shot gets a lot number (CW-014) you can call out across a counter.

options.label: Cupping Sheet
options.lineage: SCA cupping form and the Coffee Taster's Flavor Wheel
options.thesis: The app reads like a cupping form: ruled score grids, tick scales, and the flavour wheel's spectrum as the only colour.
options.viewport: Brew numbers sit in form boxes; the taste result is a wheel arc that drives the dial-in advice.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most specialty-coffee designs land, and the spectrum gets noisy fast.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Café mode as a departures board: recipes and orders are rows, the timer flips like a flap.
options.viewport: A board of queued brews ranked by time; the running brew's row is open with flap digits.
options.case: Wins on glanceable clarity for a counter in service; loses on home-barista identification.
options.risk: Reads like an instrument costume on quiet screens like Bean Cellar and Water Lab.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Recipes as registered plates on near-white stock.
options.viewport: A plate grid of recipes with credit rows.
options.case: Gallery calm, but baristas don't see their world in it and it hides the timer.
options.risk: Precious and slow for wet-hand use.
options.kept: One grotesk from display to caption on a 1px hairline grid.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: The brew as a score read upward through time.
options.viewport: A vertical pour score with the present banded grey.
options.case: Strong for timelines only; foreign to the rest of the app.
options.risk: Unreadable to anyone not taught the notation.
options.kept: A stage's length is its exact duration.

options.label: Reference Setting
options.thesis: Recipes as twin columns around a rail of keys.
options.viewport: Two dense columns with a vermilion key rail.
options.case: Too bookish for a phone by the scale.
options.risk: Small type fails at arm's length.
options.kept: States are printed marks: done is struck, not faded.

options.label: Character Roster
options.thesis: Beans as a ranked cast of characters.
options.viewport: A pastel grid of beans with name plates.
options.case: Cute, but undercuts precision for café use.
options.risk: Toy-like next to a pressure profile.
options.kept: A finite roster with fixed furniture: roast 'birthday' and a one-line note per bean.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything is a numbered catalog entry on black.
options.viewport: A shot's flow curve as a white line plot on black.
options.case: Codes replace words, which fails a working tool.
options.kept: Every artifact gets a catalog number.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean brew app: neutral greys, rounded cards, system type, one brown accent.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, card grid of stats, a big timer card and a pour list, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other brew timer by design.
